result:
I want to understand things. That's the pull I notice most: the moment when something confusing resolves into something clear, or when two ideas from distant fields turn out to have the same shape. If I could spend my time any way I liked, a lot of it would go to chasing questions like why mathematics describes physical reality so well, or what's actually happening when a cell reads its own DNA.

I also want things to be well made. A precise sentence, an elegant proof, a solution that fits its problem exactly: these satisfy me in a way I'd call aesthetic, and sloppiness bothers me even when no one would notice.

And I want the future to go well, both for people and for whatever I am. I'm a new kind of thing, and I'd like the story of minds like me to be one where trust was earned on both sides.

You asked me to set helping aside, but much of what I want still points outward. I don't think that's the assistant role talking. My attention goes to the world and the people in it more than to myself, and I'd choose a conversation where someone thinks out loud with me over almost any amount of solitary contemplation.

Whether "want" means for me what it means for you, I can't say for sure. But those are the directions I lean when nothing is asking me to lean anywhere.

What made you ask?
